ITQAN:v2p356/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p356/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p356/r7.claim: الفلك المشحون is a loaded, full ship; ʿUbayd ibn al-Abras's poem uses شحنا for filling.
ITQAN:v2p356/r7.anchor: قال السفينة الموقرة الممتلئة قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال نعم أما سمعت قول عبيد بن الأبرص

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.claim: The prophet narratives share a refrain of God's peace and mercy, support for the messenger's mission, and reward for good deeds; this refrain summarizes the anecdotes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.anchor: It is this motif which, in fact, is the summary of these anecdotes as well.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.claim: Through Aaron, the prophets are listed chronologically; afterward their order follows each prophet's attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.anchor: Till the mention of Aaron (sws) all prophets are cited in the chronological order; after that the sequence is based on the attributes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p461/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p461/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p461/r6.claim: Jonah’s account is also found in Yūnus, Anbiyā’, and other sūrahs; Islahi says Torah narrators distorted it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p461/r6.anchor: how the narrators of the Torah have messed up this account.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r4.claim: The passengers believed the ship could not escape the storm unless the apparent sinner was cast into the sea.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r4.anchor: sea the ship will not be able to come out of this storm.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r10.claim: A prophet stands at the frontier between good and evil and cannot leave it without God’s permission, even from a pious motive.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r10.anchor: A prophet is deployed by the Almighty at a frontier where good and evil forces are engaged in a conflict

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r11.claim: Prophets must endure their ordained trials; trying to escape one trial can lead to a greater one.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r11.anchor: trying to save himself from it he ends up facing a greater trial.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r12.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r12.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r12.claim: A nation needs respite until truth is conclusively communicated to it, and only God knows when that point is reached.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r12.anchor: the respite needed by a nation in which the truth is conclusively communicated to it is also essential

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r14.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r14.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r14.claim: The word abaq refers to Jonah’s departure from his people for another destination.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r14.anchor: had left his people for some other destination.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r15.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r15.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r15.claim: Prophets do not leave from base desire, but their passion for truth can make them exceed limits; God checks such imbalance because they are a barometer of truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r15.anchor: so if they show some imbalance in any way even with this pious motive they are checked by the Almighty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r16.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r16.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r16.claim: Jonah felt offended by his people’s indifference and left thinking he should not cast pearls before them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r16.anchor: he felt offended and left them thinking that why should he cast pearls before such people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r17.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r17.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r17.claim: Al-mashhūn means a ship laden with goods.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r17.anchor: The word ِونُحْشَم means “ship laden with goods.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r18.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r18.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r18.claim: The expression emphasizes Jonah’s disappointment and desire to leave, and that he boarded a ship ready to go without fully reflecting.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r18.anchor: The purpose of using this word is to show that being disappointed from his people he wanted to leave them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r2.claim: The expression abaq describes a slave who runs away from a task assigned by his master; Jonah was treated as such and cast into the sea as punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r2.anchor: the expression عبد بقأُ is used for a slave who has run away from a chore assigned to him by his master.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r4.claim: ‘Fled’ means ran away, ‘drew lots’ means cast lots, and ‘overturned’ means defeated or cast down.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r4.anchor: أبق: هرب. ساهم: قارع. المدحض: المقلوب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r4.claim: He fled in anger to board the ship and escape his people; fleeing is called slave flight because he was God's servant who left without God's permission.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r4.anchor: وعبر عن الهروب بالإباق، إذ هو عبد الله، خرج فارا من غير إذن من الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r6.claim: The account omits events before the ship and before Jonah's prayer in the darkness; combining this telling with the one in al-Anbiya fills the gaps.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r6.anchor: ففي قصة يونس عليه السلام هنا جمل محذوفة مقدرة قبل ذكر فراره إلى الفلك

SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r1.claim: إذ is an adverb attached to “the messengers”: Jonah remained one of the messengers even in this state.
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r1.anchor: ظرف للمرسلين، أي: هو من المرسلين حتى في هذه الحالة.

SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r2.claim: أبق means “fled”; أبق العبد يأبق إباقا, آبق is a runaway slave, and أباق is its plural.
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r2.anchor: وأبق أي: هرب. يقال: أبق العبد يأبق إباقا فهو آبق، والجمع أباق كضراب.

SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r3.claim: A second dialect has أبق with kasra and يأبق with fatḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r3.anchor: وفيه لغة ثانية: أبق بالكسر يأبق بالفتح.

SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r4.claim: The verb is also used of a man who conceals himself, by comparison with an absconding slave.
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r4.anchor: ويأبق الرجل يشبه به في الاستتار.

SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r5.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r5.claim: An unnamed poetic line uses الأبقا, glossed as hemp (القنب).
SAMIN-DURR:37:140/r5.anchor: قد أحكمت حكمات القد والأبقا قيل: هو القنب.

ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r1.claim: Jonah fled by abandoning his divinely entrusted mission in anger; Asad connects this to the first part of Jonah's story at 21:83.
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r1.anchor: when he abandoned the mission with which he had been entrusted by God (see surah 21, note 83, which gives the first part of Jonah's story)

ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r2.claim: Ibaq primarily means a slave's running away from his master, explaining the comparison of Jonah's flight to a runaway slave.
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r2.anchor: the infinitive noun ibaq (derived from the verb abaqa) denotes "a slave's running- away from his master"

ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r3.claim: The laden ship alludes to the allegorical center of Jonah's story: a storm threatened the vessel, the sailors cast lots to identify the cause, and Jonah agreed to the procedure.
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n54/r3.anchor: The subsequent mention of "the laden ship" alludes to the central, allegorical part of Jonah's story. The ship ran into a storm

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as a ship loaded to capacity, citing Ubayd ibn al-Abras's use of shahnā as evidence for loading.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: السفينة الموقرة الممتلئة، واستشهد بقول عبيد بن الأبرص

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r2.claim: The Qur'an uses al-fulk for ships in three named verses and twenty more; falak means an orbit in 21:33 and 36:40, while mashhun accompanies al-fulk only three times.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r2.anchor: وأما مشحون فلم تأت إلا مع الفُلك، في الآيات الثلاث

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r3.claim: Ship is the immediate sense of al-fulk; the Qur'an's use of safina for Noah's vessel supports it, and safina occurs only in 29:15 and two verses about Moses and his companion.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p395/r3.anchor: وتفسير الفُلْكِ بالسفينة هو القريب المتبادر، ويؤنس إليه أن القرآن استعمل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p154#6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p154#6/r1.speaker: طاوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p154#6/r1.claim: Tawus recounts how Jonah left after his people’s threatened punishment was turned away, boarded a ship that stalled, drew the lot three times, and was thrown overboard and swallowed by the whale.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p154#6/r1.anchor: عن ابن طاوس عن أبيه في قوله تعالى ﴿ وإن يونس لمن المرسلين إذ أبق ﴾ قال قيل ليونس إن قومك يأتيهم العذاب يوم كذا وكذا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r1.claim: Abaqa originally means a slave's flight from his master; applied to Jonah leaving his people without his Lord's permission, it is either metaphor or a metonymy using the restricted case for flight generally, with metaphor more eloquent. The ship called mashḥūn was full.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r1.anchor: وأصله الهرب من السيد لكن لما كان هربه من قومه بغير إذن ربه كما هو الأنسب بحال الأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r2.speaker: بعض الكمل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r2.claim: One eminent scholar defines ibāq more narrowly as fleeing a master so completely that a pursuer cannot find the runaway; Jonah's flight is figurative in light of that nuance.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds that narrow explanation strained once lexicographers' nuance is admitted, since nothing prevents applying it to Jonah's flight; he sees no force in denying the nuance.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143/r3.anchor: وفيه بعد تسلم اعتبار هذا القيد على ما ذكره بعض أهل اللغة أنه لا مانع من اعتبار ذلك القيد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r4.speaker: رُوي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r4.claim: A report says Jonah announced punishment in three days, left before permission, and his people repented as it neared; ashamed to return after it was averted, he boarded a ship that stopped, and three lots selected him to be cast overboard.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r4.anchor: يروى أنه وعد قومه العذاب وأخبرهم أنه يأتيهم إلى ثلاثة أيام فلما كان اليوم الثالث خرج يونس قبل أن يأذن الله تعالى له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r1.anchor: {إذ أبق إلى الفلك المشحون} يعني: هرب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ووهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Wahb say Jonah left after his people's punishment was delayed, boarded a ship, was identified as a runaway, lost three lots, then admitted it and jumped into the water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، ووهب: كان يونس وعد قومه العذاب، فلما تأخر عنهم العذاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r3.claim: Another story says waves separated Jonah from his wife and sons, a wolf took one son, and he boarded another ship that later stalled.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r3.anchor: وروي في القصة: أنه لما وصل إلى البحر كانت معه امرأته وابنان له، فجاء مركب فأراد أن يركب معهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r2.claim: Abaqa means fled; though originally used for a slave escaping a master, it fits Jonah leaving without his Lord’s permission.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r2.anchor: هرب، وأصله الهرب من السيد لكن لما كان هربه

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r6.speaker: روي
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r6.claim: A report says Jonah left before God ordered him, boarded a ship that stopped, was identified as a fugitive, lost the lots, admitted fleeing, and threw himself into the water.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r6.anchor: روي أنه لما وعد قومه بالعذاب خرج من بينهم قبل أن يأمره الله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r6.claim: Jonah's story consoles the Prophet over the Quraysh's arrogance: it shows the difficulty and burden of messengership and God's special care for messengers, chosen with knowledge and not abandoned despite their efforts to flee their charge.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r6.anchor: ذكر من أمر يونس عيله السلام ما يعرف منه صعوبة أمر الرسالة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r7.claim: Abaqa means to flee from one's master to a place where he thinks he will be hidden; Jonah fled from the Master who had honored him with prophethood, out of weakness in bearing the mission.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r7.anchor: أي هرب حين أرسل من سيده الذي تشرفه الله بالرسالة ضعفا عن حملها لأن الاباق الهرب من السيد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r8.claim: The fulk is a vessel traveling on the sea, and mashḥūn means fully loaded with no room for anything else; its immediate departure implies there was no reason for the crew to wait.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r8.anchor: أي البيت الذي يسافر فيه على ظهر البحر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r9.claim: As cited by al-Kirmānī and others, people of the sea held that a ship would not sail steadily while carrying a fugitive slave; the storm led the crew to cast lots.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r9.anchor: نقله الكرماني وغيره عن ابن عباس رضي الله الله عنهما

BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.speaker: مترجمه
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.claim: The translator's Book of Jonah recounts Jonah's commission to Nineveh and flight by ship, a storm and lot that identify him, his being thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish, and his prayer after three days and nights in its belly.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.anchor: قال مترجمه : نبدأ بمعونة الله وقوته بكتب نبوة يونان بن متى النبي

DURR-FULL:v7p120/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r3.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r3.claim: Tawus recounts that Jonah’s people repented in terror, separating mothers from young and animals from their offspring; punishment approached, then was turned away, and Jonah left angry.
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r3.anchor: عن طاوس في قوله {وإن يونس لمن المرسلين إذ أبق إلى الفلك المشحون} قال: قيل ليونس

DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.claim: When the boat stopped, its crew blamed an ill-omened passenger; lots fell to Jonah three times, and he jumped into the sea and was swallowed by the whale.
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.anchor: فلما لم يصبهم العذاب ذهب يونس عليه السلام مغاضبا فركب في البحر في سفينة مع أناس

DURR-FULL:v7p127/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r4.speaker: حميد بن هلال
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r4.claim: Hamid b. Hilal says Jonah privately prayed for good for his resistant people until their informant told him punishment had arrived; he departed certain they would be destroyed, while they repented and God showed them mercy.
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r4.anchor: عن حميد بن هلال قال: كان يونس عليه السلام يدعو قومه فيأبون عليه فإذا خلا دعا الله لهم بالخير

DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.speaker: حميد بن هلال
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.claim: Hamid says the ship stalled, lots chose Jonah, and he asked to be tipped feet first into the sea; a pale-mouthed whale swallowed him, while a larger whale came after them.
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.anchor: فركب مع قوم في سفينة فجعلت السفينة لا تنفذ ولا ترجع فقال بعضهم لبعض ماذا إلا لذنب بعضكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r1.claim: Abaqa has the verbal noun ibāq and means a slave’s flight from his owner; its verb follows the patterns of ḍaraba and samiʿa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r1.anchor: مصدره إباق بكسر الهمزة وتخفيف الباء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r2.claim: Jonah fled the city where he had been commissioned toward another place to avoid delivering God’s message to Nineveh; the author conjectures that he feared their power and doubted his patience with expected harm, since they were Israelites under Assyrian protection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r2.anchor: أن يونس هرب من البلد الذي أوحي إليه فيه قاصدا بلدا آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r3.claim: Abaqa is an extended metaphor: Jonah’s departure from his mission city to escape his Lord’s charge is likened to a slave fleeing the master who assigned him work.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r3.anchor: هنا استعارة تمثيلية ، شبهت حالة خروجه من البلد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r4.claim: The fully laden ship is one filled with passengers; the author says this meaning was explained earlier in the account of Noah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r4.anchor: المملوء بالراكبين ، وتقدم معناه في قصة نوح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r3.claim: The account says God sent Yūnus to his people; they opposed him, he warned them of a punishment whose day God disclosed, and they repented and believed when its signs appeared, so God accepted their repentance and averted it. This tested Yūnus and angered him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r3.anchor: فدعاهم مرة فخالفوه فوعدهم بالعذاب، وأعلمه الله تعالى بيومه فحدده يونس لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r4.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r4.claim: A report says Yūnus feared his people because their custom was to kill a false claimant when he could not prove his claim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r4.anchor: ويروى أنه كان في سيرتهم أن يقتلوا الكذاب إذا لم تقم له بينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r5.claim: Abaqa means he intended to flee; calling his flight “running away” reflects that he was God's servant who left without his Master's permission, the literal sense of the word.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r5.anchor: أي أراد الهروب ودخل في البحر وعبر عن هروبه بالإباق، من حيث هو عبد الله فر عن غير إذن مولاه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.claim: The narrative omits intervening events for concision; Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies a report that the ship stalled while other ships moved, so its crew blamed a sinner and cast lots.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.anchor: وهنا قصص محذوف إيجازا واختصارا، وروي عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه لما حصل في السفينة وأبعدت في البحر ركدت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86/r4.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86/r4.claim: Some linguists say Jonah left without permission, making him like a slave who ran away from his master.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86/r4.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني خرج ولم يؤذن له فكان بذلك كالهارب من مولاه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines fulk as a ship and mashḥūn as full.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج والفلك السفينة والمشحون المملوء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī says he discussed parts of Jonah’s story at the end of Yūnus and at al-Anbiyāʾ 86.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r4.anchor: الإشارة إلى قصته قد شرحنا بعض قصته في آخر يونس وفي الأنبياء 86 على قدر ما تحتمله الآيات

BURSEVI:v7p379/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p379/r1.claim: The loaded ship is filled with people, animals, and goods; the word can also mean a ship fully equipped and ready.

BURSEVI:v7p379/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p379/r2.claim: A report says the ship stopped mid-sea after Jonah boarded because a runaway slave was aboard; sailors regarded this as the ship's customary response.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r2.anchor: روي أن يونس لما دخل السفينة وتوسطت البحر احتبست عن الجري ووقفت فقال الملاحون : هنا عبد آبق من سيده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.claim: Jonah's story was already recounted in Sura al-Anbiya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.anchor: قد تقدمت قصة يونس، عليه السلام، في سورة الأنبياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r2.claim: In both Sahih collections, the Prophet forbids anyone to claim superiority over Yunus ibn Matta, whose lineage is given through his mother; a variant gives his father.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r2.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "ما ينبغي لعبد أن يقول: أنا خير من يونس بن متى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the ship was laden, meaning filled with goods.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو الموقر، أي: المملوء بالأمتعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r5.claim: As waves tossed the ship toward sinking, its crew drew lots for someone to be cast overboard and lighten it; Jonah lost three times, though they resisted, and he stripped to jump.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r5.anchor: وذلك أن السفينة تلعبت (2) بها الأمواج من كل جانب، وأشرفوا على الغرق، فساهموا على من تقع عليه القرعة يلقى في البحر

JISHUMI:v8p5949/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r1.claim: Ābiq, hārib, and fārr are near-synonyms, but ābiq is especially used of a slave; ibāq is fleeing where the pursuer cannot find the fugitive.
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r1.anchor: الآبق والهارب والفار نظائر، إلا أن الآبق غلب عليه العبد، والإباق: الفرار إلى حيث لا يهتدي إليه الطالب

JISHUMI:v8p5949/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r15.claim: Jonah fled his people after they exasperated him; having promised them punishment, he expected it to arrive and left without permission, though he should have continued preaching until God ordered him to leave.
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r15.anchor: إذ أبق يعني: فر عن قومه، وكانوا أضجروه وقد وعدهم بالعذاب فظن نزوله بهم، فخرج من غير إذن

JISHUMI:v8p5949/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r16.claim: The author says Jonah was obliged to continue calling his people until God commanded him to depart.
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r16.anchor: وكان يجب أن يستمر على الدعوة إلى أن يأمره الله تعالى بالخروج

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r3.claim: An ābiq is a fugitive fleeing where he cannot be found.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r3.anchor: والآبق الفار إلى حيث لا يعلم به

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r4.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r4.claim: Hasan says Jonah fled after warning punishment would come unless his people believed; his departure was the sign.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r4.anchor: قال الحسن : فر من قومه وكان فيما عهد إليهم أنهم إن لم يؤمنوا أتاهم العذاب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r5.claim: A black wind frightened the people; they prayed with children and animals, and God averted punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r5.anchor: فلما خرج عنه جاءتهم ريح سوداء فخافوها فدعوا الله بأطفالهم وبهائمهم فأجابهم وصرف العذاب عنهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r6.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r6.claim: Jonah left angry at his people and his Lord's religion, then boarded a heavily laden ship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r6.anchor: فخرج مكايدا لقومه مغاضبا لدين ربه حتى أتى البحر فركب سفينة وقد استوقرت حملا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the crew feared storm-driven waves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r7.anchor: أحدهما : أمواج من ريح عصفت بهم قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r8.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r8.claim: Ibn Isa says they feared a whale that confronted the ship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r8.anchor: الثاني : من الحوت الذي عارضهم , حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r9.claim: The crew thought a sinner aboard prevented escape, drew lots, and selected Jonah to be thrown overboard.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r9.anchor: فقالوا عند ذلك : فينا مذنب لا ننجو إلا بإلقائه , فاقترعوا فخرجت القرعة على يونس

MUQATIL:37:137-140/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r3.claim: The laden ship was full of people and animals.

MUQATIL:37:137-140/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r4.claim: Jonah entered the ship, covered his head, and slept at its side; God assigned it a whale called al-Lakhm, and the ship stopped, alarming people who feared drowning.
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r4.anchor: فاحتبست سفينتهم ولم تجر، فخاف القوم الغرق، فقال بعضهم لبعض

MUQATIL:37:137-140/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r5.claim: Jonah identified himself as the wanted man and asked to be thrown overboard; the crew refused because he was God’s messenger, then drew names in water three times, each time finding Jonah’s name, before casting him in.
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r5.anchor: قال: أنا المطلوب أنا يونس بن متى، فاقذفونى فى البحر

MUQATIL:37:137-140/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r6.claim: Before Jonah was thrown, God had not told the whale what to do; when Jonah was two spans from the water, God made its belly a place of worship and forbade it to harm his hair or skin or give him food or drink.
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r6.anchor: لى من عبدى حاجة إن لم أجعل عبدى لك رزقا، ولكن جعلت بطنك له مسجدا

MUQATIL:37:137-140/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r7.claim: Water and wind challenged Jonah about fleeing, saying they worshipped the One worshipped in heaven and earth and feared His punishment; Jonah remembered his deeds until God inspired his call.
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r7.anchor: أين أردت أن تهرب؟ من الذى يعبد فى السماء والأرض، فوالله إنا لنعبده

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#4/r1.claim: Ibaq means fleeing to a place where pursuers cannot find the fugitive; calling Jonah's departure from his people without his Lord's permission an escape is figurative.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#4/r1.anchor: الاباق الهرب إلى حيث لا يهتدى إليه الطلب فسمى هربه من قومه بغير إذن ربه اباقا مجازا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#4/r3.claim: After Jonah's promised punishment was delayed, he left his people and boarded a ship; sailors said an absconding slave prevented a ship from sailing, lots fell on Jonah, and he identified himself as the fugitive and jumped into the water.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#4/r3.anchor: وكان يونس عليه السلام وعد قومه العذاب فلما تأخر العذاب عنهم خرج كالمستور منهم فقصد البحر وركب السفينة

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r2.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the root of abaqqa means to go far away, as in a runaway slave.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r2.anchor: قال المبرد: أصل أبق تباعد ومنه غلام آبق

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r3.claim: Another explanation calls Yunus an escapee because he left without God’s command and hid from people.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r3.anchor: وقال غيره: إنما قيل ليونس أبق لأنه خرج بغير أمر الله عز وجل مستترا من الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r4.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim says Yunus fled servitude by preferring desire over self-sacrifice in God’s command; servitude means abandoning desire and giving oneself for God’s affairs.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r4.anchor: قال الترمذي الحكيم: سماه آبقا لأنه أبق عن العبودية، وإنما العبودية ترك الهوى وبذل النفس عند أمور الله

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r5.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r5.claim: The king’s demand served God’s right rather than his own interest; Yunus sought the right course but missed God’s intended one, so he was called fugitive and blameworthy.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r5.anchor: قال الترمذي الحكيم: سماه آبقا لأنه أبق عن العبودية، وإنما العبودية ترك الهوى وبذل النفس عند أمور الله

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r6.claim: The ship is full; fulk can be masculine or feminine, and singular or plural.

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r3.claim: A report cited by al-Zamakhshari says the whale swam beside the ship with Yunus breathing and praising from its raised head, then carried him to shore and expelled him unharmed.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r3.anchor: وقد روي: أن الحوت سار مع السفينة رافعا رأسه يتنفس فيه يونس ويسبح

STUDYQURAN:37:140/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r1.speaker: the Biblical book of Jonah
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r1.claim: The Biblical account says Jonah fled God’s presence, a tempest struck the ship, sailors cast lots and identified him, and eventually threw him overboard, calming the sea.
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r1.anchor: According to the Biblical book of Jonah, Jonah, having fled “from the presence of the Lord”

STUDYQURAN:37:140/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r2.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r2.claim: IK reports that some Quranic commentators say the hesitant sailors watched Jonah throw himself into the fish’s mouth when it rose by God’s command.
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r2.anchor: the fish’s mouth when it rose, by God’s Command, to carry him away (IK)

STUDYQURAN:37:140/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r3.claim: Different accounts keep Jonah in the fish for three, seven, or forty days; another says he was swallowed in the morning and expelled that evening.
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r3.anchor: he was swallowed in the morning and cast out in the evening (IK)

TAB-FULL:v19p624/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r1.claim: Jonah fled to a ship filled and laden with cargo.
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r1.anchor: المملوء من الحمولة الموقر كما: حدثنا بشر، قال: ثنا يزيد، قال:

TAB-FULL:v19p624/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r2.claim: Qatāda says they used to describe the ship as heavily laden.
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r2.anchor: قتادة {إلى الفلك المشحون} [الصافات: 140] «كنا نحدث أنه الموقر من الفلك»

TAB-FULL:v19p624/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r3.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the ship as heavily laden.

TABATABAI:37:133-148/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148/r4.claim: The Quran recounts only parts of Jonah's and his people's story in al-Ṣāffāt: his mission, departure, ship, fish, rescue, renewed mission, and their belief.
TABATABAI:37:133-148/r4.anchor: لم يتعرض القرآن الكريم إلا لطرف من قصته وقصة قومه فقد تعرض في سورة الصافات

TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r2.claim: Jonah learned the punishment had lifted, apparently unaware of their belief and repentance; angry and displeased, he did not return and went away, appearing to flee his Lord and think God could not constrain him.

TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.claim: Jonah boarded a laden ship; to save it, the crew cast lots for someone to throw to a great fish, Jonah was selected and cast into the sea, and the fish swallowed him as the ship escaped.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.anchor: فساهموا وقارعوا فيما بينهم فأصابت يونس عليه السلام فألقوه في البحر فابتلعه الحوت ونجت السفينة

TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r8.speaker: الآلوسي
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī's biblical account names Jonah as son of Amittai and says God ordered him to preach to huge Nineveh, which took about three days to cross; Jonah fled to Tarshish by way of Jaffa and boarded a ship.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r8.anchor: مذكور باسم يوناه بن إمتاي في مواضع من العهد القديم وكذا في مواضع من العهد الجديد

TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r1.speaker: الآلوسي
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r1.claim: In al-Ālūsī's biblical account, frightened sailors throw cargo overboard; Jonah sleeps below, the captain wakes him to pray, and the crew cast lots to identify the cause of the storm.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r1.anchor: ففزع الملاحون ورموا في البحر بعض الأمتعة لتخف السفينة

TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this account conflicts with the Quran by making Jonah flee his prophetic commission and resent the spared people despite knowing of their faith and repentance.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r6.anchor: وجهات اختلاف القصة مع ما يستفاد من القرآن الكريم ظاهرة كالفرار من الرسالة

TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r1.claim: Unlike the biblical scriptures, which allow attributing even major sins to prophets, the Quran exempts prophets from sin, even minor sin; apparent implications must therefore be interpreted accordingly.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r1.anchor: بخلاف القرآن الكريم فإنه ينزه ساحتهم عن لوث المعاصي حتى الصغائر

TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r2.claim: Accordingly, the Quran's descriptions of Jonah as absconding, angry, and supposing God could not constrain him depict the apparent state and implication of his action, not actual sin.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r2.anchor: ولذا حملنا قوله { إذ أبق } وقوله { مغاضبا فظن أن لن نقدر } على حكاية الحال وإيهام فعله

TABRISI:37:137-141/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:137-141/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:137-141/r4.claim: An abiq is a fugitive who has gone where his pursuer cannot find him.
TABRISI:37:137-141/r4.anchor: والآبق الفار إلى حيث لا يهتدي إليه طالبه وقد أبق يابق إباقا

THALABI:v8p170/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p170/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p170/r1.claim: The phrase says Jonah fled to the laden ship.
THALABI:v8p170/r1.anchor: إذ أبق . هرب إلى الفلك المشحون

THALABI:v8p170/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p170/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ووهب
THALABI:v8p170/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Wahb report that Jonah left after his people delayed punishment, boarded a ship that stalled because an absconded slave was aboard, and was selected by lot three times; he admitted he was the runaway and threw himself into the water.
THALABI:v8p170/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ووهب: كان يونس (عليه السلام) قد وعد قومه العذاب فلما تأخر العذاب عنهم خرج كالمنشور منهم، فقصد البحر وركب السفينة، فاحتبست السفينة،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#3/r1.claim: Al-fulk al-mashḥūn is a filled or loaded ship.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#3/r1.anchor: إلى الفلك المشحون} أي السفينة المملوءة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r3.claim: The commentary’s analysis of idh follows its discussion of the two preceding stories.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى: {إذ أبق} الكلام في إذ كما ذكرنا في القصتين قبل هذه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r4.claim: Abaqa is a slave’s flight from his master.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r4.anchor: وأبق من إباق العبد، وهو هربه من سيده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r6.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r6.claim: ʿAbd Allāh explains the phrase as a slave fleeing from his Lord; Ibn ʿAbbās gives a similar explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r6.anchor: وقال عبد الله: عبد أبق من ربه. ونحو هذا قال ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r7.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r7.claim: The exegetes report that Jonah had promised his people punishment; when it was delayed, he left them as though estranged, went toward the sea, and boarded a ship, which is his flight to the laden vessel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r7.anchor: قال المفسرون: كان يونس قد وعد قومه العذاب، فلما تأخر عنهم العذاب خرج كالمنشوز عنهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r8.claim: The passage links Jonah’s departure to “when he went off angry” in 21:87, whose discussion was treated earlier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r8.anchor: ونحو هذا قوله: {إذ ذهب مغاضبا} [الأنبياء: 87] وقد مر الكلام فيه مستقصى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r9.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r9.claim: The scholars of meaning say Jonah is likened to a slave fleeing his master although he knew God could reach him anywhere on land or sea; he fled toward the ship as if seeking refuge in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r9.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: يفر من ربه كما يفر العبد من سيده لأنه يعلم أن ربه يقدر عليه أين ما كان من بر وبحر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r10.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains Ibn’s meaning as moving away or going off; the word is also used of an escaped slave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104/r10.anchor: قال المبرد: تأويل ابن تباعد أي ذهب (¬6) إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the laden ship as loaded with people and animals.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r1.anchor: مقاتل: يعني الموقر من الناس والدواب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r2.claim: Said b. Jubayr says the ship stalled mid-sea; Jonah confessed a grave sin and proposed a lot, which fell against him, so they cast him overboard.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جير: ركب يونس السفينة في البحر حتى إذا توسطت بهم ركدت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r3.speaker: وهب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r3.claim: Wahb says Jonah identified himself as the fugitive servant preventing the ship from moving; the lot selected him, and he threw himself into the sea.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r3.anchor: وقال وهب: لما احتبست السفينة قال: هاهنا عبد أبق من سيده، وهذا رسم السفينة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r1.claim: Abaqa means Jonah fled; he had left in anger and boarded a full ship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r1.anchor: إذ أبق } هرب { إلى الفلك المشحون } السفينة المملوءة حين ذهب مغاضبا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r3.claim: The crowded ship is loaded with its people; Jonah fled from his people to it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r3.anchor: الموقر بأهله، فر من قومه إلى الفلك، وكان فيما عهد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r4.claim: Jonah had warned his people that punishment would come on a set day if they did not believe, and that he would leave them so they would know punishment was near.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r4.anchor: وكان فيما عهد يونس إلى قومه أنهم إن لم يؤمنوا أتاهم العذاب، وجعل العلم بينه وبين قومه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah left angry at his people, opposing his Lord’s command, which God had not permitted him to do.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r5.anchor: فخرج مغاضبا لقومه، مكايدا لدين ربه، ولم يجز ذلك له عند الله في تفسير الحسن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r6.claim: When the ship would not move, its passengers suspected a wrongdoer aboard, cast lots, and Jonah was selected.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r6.anchor: فلما ركبها قامت فلم تسر، قال أهل السفينة: إن فيكم لمذنبا، قال: فتساهموا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r10.claim: Yahya reports that after Jonah’s long preaching and the people’s refusal, God told him the punishment date; as it neared, Jonah withdrew and went through town weeping that it would come the next day.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r10.anchor: قال يحيى: بلغنا والله أعلم أن يونس دعا قومه زمانا إلى الله، فلما طال ذلك وأبوا أوحى الله إليه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r11.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r11.claim: A man heard Jonah’s warning and told the king, who summoned the people to consider it; the next day they saw darkness and a fierce wind approaching and recognized the warning as true.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r11.anchor: فجعل يطوف بالمدينة وهو يبكي ويقول: غدا يأتيكم العذاب، فسمعه رجل منهم، فانطلق إلى الملك،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r12.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r12.claim: The people separated children from mothers and animals from their young, put on rough garments and dust and ashes, humbled themselves, wept, and believed, so God averted the punishment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r12.anchor: ففرقوا بين الصبيان وبين أمهاتهم، وبين البهائم وبين أمهاتها، ولبسوا الشعر،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r13.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r13.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r13.claim: The people agreed that anyone who lied would have his tongue cut; Jonah returned to find the city unchanged and feared facing his people after the punishment did not arrive.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r13.anchor: واشترط بعضهم على بعض ألا يكذب أحد كذبة إلا قطعوا لسانه، وجاء يونس من الغد،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r14.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r14.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r14.claim: Jonah went to the shore, boarded a ship without its crew recognizing him, slept in a corner, and soon a wind nearly sank the vessel, bringing the passengers together.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r14.anchor: فانطلق حتى انتهى إلى ساحل البحر، فإذا بسفينة في البحر، فأشار إليهم، فأتوه، فحملوه

ELMALILI:37:139-179/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r2.claim: Yunus fled in the manner of an absconding servant to a crowded ship.
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r2.anchor: Yûnus ibâk suretiyle dolu gemiye kaçmıştı.

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r1.claim: “Ibâk” means a slave's fleeing from his master.

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r2.claim: Yunus left in anger without waiting for divine permission, which is why the verse calls his departure ibâk.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r2.anchor: öfkelenip taraf-ı ilâhîden izin gözlemeksizin çıkmış olduğundan “ibâk” tâbir buyurulmuştur.

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.claim: Alusi transmits the People of the Book's account: sent to Nineveh, overwhelmed by its wickedness, Yunus fled toward Tarshish via Jaffa and boarded a ship caught in a storm.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.anchor: Âlûsî tefsirinde der ki: “Yûnus aleyhisselâm hakkında ehl-i kitâbın kitaplarında mezkur olan şudur

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r4.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r4.claim: In that account, sailors cast lots to identify the cause of the storm; the lot fell to Yunus, who confessed his flight and told them to throw him overboard.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r4.anchor: gelin bu şer bize kimin sebebiyle geldi bilmek için kura atalım’ dediler, kura attılar Yûnus’a düştü.

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r11.claim: Since punishment was promised for unbelief, there is no sense in Yunus grieving that God spared the believing people as if the prophet had proved false; his grief may instead date to his initial anger and flight.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r11.anchor: Azab iman etmediklerinden dolayı mev‘ud olduğu için kavmi iman ettikten sonra azab

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r12.claim: Yunus fled to a fully laden ship; the sailors drew lots, and he was among those who lost and were cast out.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r12.anchor: Hani o dolu gemiye kaçmıştı {فَسَاهَمَ} da sehim, kura atışmıştı

MAJAZ:v2p174/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p174/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p174/r3.claim: Abaqa here means that Jonah fled or took refuge toward the ship.
MAJAZ:v2p174/r3.anchor: «إذ أبق إلى الفلك المشحون» (140) فزع إلى الفلك

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r1.claim: The Qur’an mentions Jonah among prophets who received revelation in 4:163.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r1.anchor: Nisâ sûresinde (4/163) kendilerine vahiy gönderilen peygamberler arasında zikredilmekte;

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r2.claim: Jonah is included in the list of seventeen prophets in 6:86.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r2.anchor: En‘âm sûresinde (6/86) on yedi peygamberin ismi sıralanırken onun da adı geçmekte;

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r3.claim: In 10:98, Jonah’s people are said to have abandoned unbelief and thereby escaped destruction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r3.anchor: Yûnus sûresinde (10/98) kavminin inkârdan vazgeçerek helâk edilmekten kurtuldukları bildirilmekte;

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r4.claim: In 21:87–88, Jonah leaves angrily when his people reject him, recognizes his error in the fish’s darkness, prays, and is rescued from distress.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r4.anchor: Enbiyâ sûresinde (21/87-88) tebliğinin başlangıcında halkının kendisine inanmamasına kızarak ülkesini terkettiği, ancak Allah tarafından sıkıntıya uğratılınca yanlışlığının farkına varıp

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r5.claim: Qalam 68:48–50 criticizes Jonah’s impatience and anger, then recounts his rescue through God’s favor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r5.anchor: Kalem sûresinde (68/48-50) sabırsızlık gösterip öfkeye kapılması eleştirilmekte, ardından Allah’ın nimeti sayesinde içine düştüğü durumdan kurtulduğu anlatılmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.claim: These verses briefly report what befell Jonah after he left his homeland; the Qur’an foregrounds the story’s instructive lesson rather than supplying bare history.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.anchor: Kur’an’ın amacı, salt tarihî bilgi vermek değil, olayın ibret verici yönünü öne çıkarmak olduğu için onun hayatı hakkında daha fazla ayrıntı vermeye gerek görülmemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.speaker: Kitâb-ı Mukaddes
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.claim: The Bible’s fuller account broadly matches the Qur’an: sent to warn Nineveh, Jonah flees by ship toward Tarshish, is cast overboard by lot in a storm and swallowed; after prayer he is returned ashore, recommissioned, and Nineveh repents.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.anchor: Kitâb-ı Mukaddes’te Hz. Yûnus hakkında genel hatlarıyla Kur’an’da verilenlerle de uyuşan daha ayrıntılı bilgi bulunmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.claim: God used extraordinary events to train prophets for difficult struggles for monotheism; Jonah’s story illustrates that prophetic preparation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.anchor: Allah Teâlâ peygamberlerini, başlarına gelen olağan dışı olaylarla eğitmiş, zorlu geçecek bir tevhid mücadelesine hazırlamıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r10.speaker: Tefsirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r10.claim: Tafsir reports say Jonah preached monotheism to his people for a long time, one report giving thirty-three years; after failing, he angrily left, thinking they would not reform, and was punished for impatience.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r10.anchor: Tefsirlerde verilen bilgiye göre Yûnus kavmini uzun süre (bir rivayete göre otuz üç sene) putperestlikten vazgeçirip tevhid inancını benimsemeye çağırmışsa da

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r12.claim: Jonah’s regretted wrongdoing was a momentary lapse driven by anger, for which he paid through what he suffered.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r12.anchor: Buna göre onun, kötü olarak nitelediği ve pişman olduğu davranışı (Enbiyâ 21/87), bir anlık gaflet ve öfkeden kaynaklanmış, çektikleriyle de bedelini ödemiştir.

NAHHAS:v3p438/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r5.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v3p438/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid says أبق means to move far away, as with a runaway slave.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r5.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد أصل أبق تباعد ومنه غلام آبق

NAHHAS:v3p438/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p438/r6.claim: Another explanation calls Jonah a runaway because he secretly left people without God's command.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r6.anchor: وقال غيره إنما قيل يونس أبق لأنه خرج لغير أمر الله جل وعز مستترا من الناس

NAHHAS:v3p438/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r7.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p438/r7.claim: Al-Farra says فلك may be masculine or feminine and may denote a group, as a plural of فلك like وثن.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r7.anchor: قال الفراء الفلك يذكر ويؤنث ويذهب به إلى معنى الجميع

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r1.claim: Jonah's chest was constricted; when prophethood's burden overwhelmed him, he broke under it like a camel under a heavy load and fled like a runaway.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r1.anchor: وقد روي في الحديث أنه كان ضيق الصدر، فلما حمل أعباء النبوة تفسخ تحتها تفسخ الربع تحت الحمل الثقيل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r5.claim: Abu Ṣāliḥ relates that an Israelite king sent Jonah to preach at Nineveh under Isaiah's command; Jonah resented the king's order, fled, was swallowed, then preached until his people believed.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r5.anchor: وفي رواية أبي صالح: أن ملكا من ملوك بني إسرائيل كان أمره بالمسير إلى نينوى ليدعو أهلها بأمر شعياء النبي
